items.title: When a young woman is raped by two friends, her small town turns against her
items.description: A local footy star and his mate are convicted of raping their friend. In the tiny town of Balmoral, where the footy club reigns, the town makes it clear whose story they believe.

items.title: Bombshell ruling by US Supreme Court kills tariffs
items.description: The US president says he is "absolutely ashamed" of members of the court who struck down his global tariffs after finding he lacked the authority to implement them.

items.title: Americans fearing death of democracy have been given a glimmer of hope
items.description: Until now, Donald Trump has been one of the most unstoppable presidents ever. But the Supreme Court's tariffs decision proves there are limits to his power.

items.title: The dirty little secret economists never want to mention
items.description: The theory goes that if you have just the right amount of workers on the unemployment scrap heap, you can keep inflation in check. The problem is that no-one knows exactly what the magic unemployment rate is.

items.title: Anna almost died in Tokyo from a disease she thought she was vaccinated against
items.description: When 24-year-old Anna Gallo woke up shivering in a Tokyo hotel, she thought it was food poisoning. Hours later, she was in a coma fighting for her life against a disease she thought she was vaccinated against.

items.title: UK to consider removing Andrew from royal succession line
items.description: The UK government is to look at removing Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor from the line of succession, an official says, as royal protection police face a grilling on "anything they saw or heard".

items.title: Should Labor have its own reshuffle?
items.description: In the past few days, in a series of largely ignored milestones overshadowed by news of Angus Taylor's new frontbench, Albanese overtook Scott Morrison and John Curtin to become the 12th-longest serving prime minister.

items.title: Four years into the war, Putin is betting on one thing
items.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin is betting that the West and Ukraine will run out of resources first.

items.title: NASA set to launch humans around Moon for first time in 50 years
items.description: NASA's Artemis II mission may launch in early March. If successful, it will be the first time humans have flown beyond the Moon in more than 50 years.

items.title: How one child had 22 foster carers by age 13 and landed in adult jail at 18
items.description: Details of a child's tumultuous journey to adulthood under the stewardship of Queensland's Department of Child Safety have been laid bare in a Toowoomba inquiry this week.

items.title: Where cameras aren't allowed, these artists become 'king'
items.description: They're a small and curious cohort in a line of work rapidly evolving. Welcome to the world of courtroom artists.

items.title: Zempilas has three H's in mind. There's one more he'll want to avoid
items.description: Housing, health and household stress — that's what WA's opposition leader says he's focused on in 2026 as he and his party face an uphill battle against the state government.

items.title: Man charged with hate crime over alleged synagogue ramming
items.description: It's alleged the 32-year-old rammed a ute into the gates of the Brisbane Synagogue on Margaret Street on Friday night.

items.title: Andy Griffiths' unlikely journey from punk rocker to children's laureate
items.description: Famous for writing stories about toilets and tree houses, the bestselling kids' author is taking on a new challenge on the national stage.

items.title: We asked for your modern dating love stories — this is what you told us
items.description: From awkward introductions over a can of soft drink to life-changing lunches, here are some of the stories ABC readers told us about their modern dating experiences.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of Ninja Turtles, Netflix and nagging pain
items.description: Every question has only two options: One is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Quick hits: Another brutal curling barb as Lindsey Vonn goes 'bionic'
items.description: Swedish curler Oskar Eriksson hits Canadian nemesis Marc Kennedy with his most devastating barb yet as Lindsey Vonn shares an update on her recovery. Here are the quick hits from day 14 at the Winter Olympics.

items.title: Epstein estate to pay up to $US35 million in victims' settlement
items.description: Jeffrey Epstein's estate has agreed to pay as much as $US35 million to resolve a class action lawsuit, according to a court filing on Thursday.

items.title: Large parts of Queensland on alert as flooding threatens to isolate communities
items.description: Flooding is likely to become more widespread in northern and western Queensland over the next few days, with further heavy rainfall and road closures expected.

items.title: 15yo one of two alleged gunmen charged over shooting of ex-NRL player
items.description: Police allege a 25-year-old man and a 15-year-old boy are responsible for the shooting of former NRL player Matt Utai outside a home in Sydney's west.

items.title: Australia blows Oman away to end T20 World Cup campaign with a bang
items.description: Australia has flogged Oman, chasing down 105 in less than 10 overs to end a disappointing World Cup campaign on a high. Follow live.

items.title: The volunteer team keeping an often-invisible global workforce afloat
items.description: In a 109-year-old building wedged between mirrored high-rises in Melbourne's CBD, a volunteer team supports a little-known workforce that spends months at a time at sea.

items.title: Growers warn 'watered down' lavender oil widespread in surging imports
items.description: Despite an Australian lavender industry dating back to the 1850s, you're more than likely using an imported and "watered-down" product, local growers say.

items.title: Rival boss says Mourinho made 'huge mistake' attacking Viní's racism claim
items.description: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany dissects the racism row involving Real Madrid and Brazil star Viní Jr with a passionate 12-minute speech.

items.title: Man Utd owner avoids sanctions over claim UK 'colonised' by immigrants
items.description: Jim Ratcliffe is reminded of his responsibilities as a participant in English football but is not handed any penalties from FA after his controversial call.
